members.name: Barbie Stockstad
members.bio: I am happy to introduce myself as part of the Anderson Island Healthcare Advocates Board. When we moved to the Island in 2014, I became well aware of the lack of healthcare services here. Having worked as a registered nurse for over 42 years, and then later as a parish nurse, it became my mission to bring services to our Island community. It takes a village of caring individuals to make this happen. I am proud to be part of a wonderful caring community that is doing just that. With my husband, Rick, we have raised 3 amazing sons and now have 7 grandchildren.

members.name: Cheryl Babo
members.bio: I have served for 2 years on the Anderson Island Health of Board Directors in 2 roles. As an island resident, it is important to me personally to serve my community in a manner that enhances all of our lives from a health and wellness perspective. With 40+ plus years' experience in the healthcare industry, I have seen what can happen when access to healthcare is compromised and unaffordable. As a healthcare leader in provider operations, health plan operations, and value-based care, it allows me to serve in a manner that positively influences the overall health and wellbeing of our Anderson Island residents. This is also why I serve on the Anderson Island Community Fitness Center as a former President and now Member-at-large.

members.name: Dianne Avey
members.bio: For over forty years Dianne Avey has worked in a variety of health care settings. She earned her undergraduate and graduate degrees from the University of Washington. Starting her career as an RN in Critical Care, she learned important skills that she used to further her career as she went on to work in Community Health, Hospice, and teaching at both Tacoma Community College and the University of Washington. Dianne returned to the UofW and completed her training as a Family Nurse Practitioner in 1990. She has worked in this role for 36yrs at a variety of primary care clinics in the Northwest. She is a long-time Island resident and a descendant of one of the pioneer families – the Ekenstams. Retiring from full-time clinical practice in 2026, she is looking forward to continuing to serve her community and use her skills as a member of the board for Anderson Island Healthcare Advocates.

members.name: Emily Martin
members.bio: I have been on the island for about ten years, living here full time since 2024. I enjoy spending time on the beach with my Labrador Retrievers, Junebug and Lazslo. Since 2003, I work in public sector labor relations, as a mediator, administrative law judge, arbitrator and trainer. I am on the leadership council of the American Bar Association's Section of Labor and Employment Law. I am also a member of Pig & Potato Games- where I work with Canadian mediators to promote collaborative culture through play.

members.name: Glenn Kasman
members.bio: I have been an Anderson Island resident since 2016 and an AIHA board member since 2023. I am a retired healthcare executive, having served as regional President for a major provider of inpatient and outpatient services in Washington State. My portfolio included leadership of hospital, clinic, physician, and health system operations as well as community relations, strategic planning and business development transactions. I began my career as a physical therapist, authored professional publications, and presented extensively in national and international settings. I have enjoyed volunteer service with local civic groups as well as professional societies, associations, and foundations with regional, national, and international reach.

members.name: Jane Fowler
members.bio: I moved to Anderson Island in 2025 and immediately felt at home here. I am a retired nurse practitioner with nearly two decades of experience working with underserved and rural communities in my home state of Wisconsin. Before that I practiced corporate law for 20+ years. I've served on the boards of several nongovernment organizations. The island's strong sense of community truly inspires me. I hope to make a positive difference in my current role as president of AIHA.

members.name: Jim Cook
members.bio: Jim is an accomplished executive and former Brigadier General whose career spans military command, high-technology leadership, and global nonprofit stewardship. In the U.S. Army Reserve, he led complex engineering, medical, and humanitarian missions, developing strategic foresight, crisis management expertise, and the ability to unify diverse teams. In the civilian sector, he served as Vice President, CTO, General Manager, and President of an international nonprofit, driving innovation, organizational transformation, and community resilience. Today, Jim applies this integrated experience to strengthen veteran support systems, empower families, and guide communities through transitioning disciplined leadership and compassionate service to every endeavor.

members.name: Michelle Ames
members.bio: With a background that blends 30 years of design with two decades of health and wellness, I've always believed that our environments and our bodies should work in harmony. As a Certified Pilates Trainer for the last 20 years I've had the privilege of helping people through restorative movement, particularly those facing neurological conditions and Scoliosis. Today, I'm leaning into my role as a connector for the Anderson Island Community Fitness Center and the Health Care Advocates. By volunteering within both of these community organizations, we will make great strides in bringing easier access to varied healthcare services for all of our neighbors.

members.name: Rick Stockstad
members.bio: After spending 45 years working in a variety of occupations (including marketing, advertising, radio, television, higher education administration, social service agency director, European tour director, and elementary music teacher!), my wife Barbie and I had the good fortune to both retire and move to Anderson Island 12 years ago. Since then we have continued to follow our passions in a number of island activities and volunteer opportunities, of which the most important and rewarding has been to help create the Anderson Island Healthcare Advocates in an effort to bring affordable and accessible healthcare to our island community.

members.name: Therese Pasquier
members.bio: Therese is a servant leader with more than 25 years of experience in healthcare administration, including roles as CEO of Sound Family Medicine and Market President of Vera Whole Health. Her career in healthcare has been matched by an equally deep commitment to community service. Over the past two decades, she has served on the boards of Good Samaritan Hospital Foundation, Emergency Food Network, St. Francis House, Riviera Community Club HOA, and Pierce College, among others. She and her husband of 32+ years moved to Anderson Island to enjoy a quieter chapter of life, but her passion for community quickly drew her back to the table. As a Board Member, she is helping to secure the resources needed to bring sustainable primary care access to island residents.
